VBO:0201068.summary: Lively and watchful, the Portuguese Podengo Pequeno retains the instincts of a rabbit hunter alongside its companion role. It searches rocky ground and dense scrub, hunting alone or in small packs. Light, agile movement is part of its working character.
VBO:0201068.shortDescription: A lively rabbit hunter and watchful companion, searching rocky ground and dense scrub alone or in small packs.

sources.title: American Kennel Club — Portuguese Podengo Pequeno standard (approved 2010; effective 2011)
sources.evidence: PDF p1 defines exact Pequeno 8–12 inches/9–13 pounds, smooth and wire coats, lean wedge head/erect ears/rectangular moderate body/sickle tail. PDF p2 Temperament describes lively rabbit hunting alone or in a small pack among rocks and thick shrub, plus companion/watchdog role; Gait describes easy, agile movements. No parent-derived behavior, ancient-origin claim or household-suitability promise.

VBO:0201387.summary: Lively and responsive with its owner, the Villano de las Encartaciones can be cautious and reserved with unfamiliar people. Its working role calls for strength and decisiveness in handling cattle. Farmers in the Encartaciones region traditionally used these dogs to catch semi-wild Monchina cattle on the mountainsides.
VBO:0201387.shortDescription: A responsive cattle-handling dog from the Encartaciones, often reserved with unfamiliar people.

sources.title: Villano de las Encartaciones — Basque standard, Order of February 15, 2018
sources.evidence: 2018Orderp1 regional origin and semi-wild Monchina capture; Annex1.3.3p5 owner-responsive cheerful/lively behavior, caution toward strangers and cattle-handling strength/decisiveness. National regional standard, not FCI status.

sources.title: Conservation of livestock genetic resources in Euskadi — Gómez and Amezaga (2003)
sources.evidence: Villano paragraph names Encartaciones/Bizkaia farmers catching semi-wild Monchina cattle in mountains. Separate Villanuco paragraph names small agile Encartaciones dog with sharp hearing, appreciated for companionship and guarding.2003 evidence; current continuity remains unqualified.

VBO:0200923.summary: Watchful and lively, Mudi tend to be keen to work, adaptable and ready to learn. These Hungarian herders have handled large, difficult livestock and also served as watch and alarm dogs. The breed took shape in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries from Hungarian herding stock, probably crossed with prick-eared German herders.
VBO:0200923.shortDescription: A lively, watchful Hungarian herder, quick to learn and keen to work; this variety has a black coat.

sources.title: FCI — Mudi standard238, official valid standard25September2023
sources.evidence: PDFp2 utilization explicitly herding large/difficult livestock, watch/alarm roles and Hungarian origin; p3 behavior lively/watchful/keen to work/adaptable/readiness to learn. Pp2/4/5 morphology wedge head/prick ears, sloping topline, smooth head/front limbs with wavy-to-curly body coat, short natural stump tails permitted, black recognized. No color-specific temperament asserted. PDFp2 historical summary explicitly dates formation to eighteenth/nineteenth centuries from Hungarian herding dogs most probably with prick-eared German herding dogs. New full copy retains probability, not a certified pedigree claim.

sources.title: FCI — current varieties of recognized breeds
sources.evidence: Mudi entry explicitly lists Black as a recognized variety. Supports exact catalog color boundary, not a separate temperament or genetically distinct breed.

VBO:0200279.summary: Balanced, watchful and patient, the Cane di Oropa is a versatile herder that learns readily and acts decisively when needed. Its work includes moving sheep between lowland and mountain pasture, guiding cattle and watching animals around farm buildings. This lean, strong Alpine dog combines courage with moderation, rather than reckless reactions.
VBO:0200279.shortDescription: A balanced, patient Alpine herder, guiding sheep and cattle with alertness, courage and a ready ability to learn.

sources.title: ENCI — Cane da Pastore di Oropa registry entry
sources.evidence: Actual ENCI entry names Cane da Pastore di Oropa admitted to RSA with recognition procedures begun; displayed905 is national entry and does not override unassigned FCI placeholders in PDF. Catalog0200279 and unselected0201457 map to same population; do not count twice.

sources.title: ENCI — Cane da Pastore di Oropa standard
sources.evidence: Complete ENCI-hosted2021 standard: history documents sheep seasonal lowland-to-mountain movement, cattle pasture and guarding animals at Alpine huts/farms. Behaviour balanced/vigilant, decision/bravery without rashness, moderation/patience and ready learning. Full and short claims supported; no parental traits, invented antiquity or FCI recognition. ENCI standard pp. 1–4 independently supports medium compact lean conformation, equal skull and muzzle lengths, small triangular erect/semi-erect/semi-dropping ears, strong tail with a scimitar repose and no curl over the back, coarse short or semi-long coat with merle allowed. Page 3 defines straight parallel forelimbs, moderate rear angulation, compact arched close-knit front toes, slightly oval hind feet and elastic pads. These conformation details supplement snow-obscured toe/contact evidence; they do not turn hidden source toes into visible ones.

VBO:0201053.summary: Friendly, lively and loyal, Miniature Poodles are active companions with a capacity for learning. Poodles were originally used to hunt waterfowl, then became popular companion dogs. Their light, bouncy movement reflects the breed’s balanced proportions.
VBO:0201053.shortDescription: A lively, loyal companion and capable learner, with waterfowl-hunting roots; this Miniature group covers grey and fawn coats.

sources.title: FCI — Poodle standard172 (2024)
sources.evidence: FCI172 (2024), p2: friendly/joyful/loyal companion character and original wildfowling work. P3: learning/training capacity and balanced proportions. P6: light, bouncy gait and grey/fawn colors (apricot/red included). P8: Miniature retains Medium proportions, over28–35cm. These are breed-level descriptions, without color-specific personality or individual guarantees.

VBO:0200570.summary: Calm and good-natured, the German Longhaired Pointer is a versatile gundog with a cooperative working character. Its work crosses field, water and forest, before and after the shot. Pure breeding dates to 1879, and a standard written in 1897 helped define the modern breed.
VBO:0200570.shortDescription: A calm, good-natured gundog with a versatile working background in fields, water and woodland.

sources.title: FCI official standard117 — German Longhaired Pointing Dog (2014)
sources.evidence: ActualPDF p2Utilization field/water/forest and before/aftershot versatilework; p2History purebreeding1879/standard1897; p2Behaviour balanced/calm/goodnatured/easilytrained. Morphology pp3–5 includes moderatelyslenderarchedmuzzle, closecoatedears, straightback and longtail withflag carriednearlyhorizontal, notcurl.

VBO:0201458.summary: Reserved with strangers and closely attached to familiar people, the Cane di Mannara tends to be calm around the animals in its care. Sicilian farms used it to guard the mannara, or sheepfold, and the flock sheltered there. Its protective work has continued against threats such as foxes and free-roaming dogs.
VBO:0201458.shortDescription: An attached but reserved Sicilian guardian, traditionally watching sheepfolds and the flocks in its care.

sources.title: Mastino Siciliano–Cane di Mannara — ENCI standard approved November 24, 2022
sources.evidence: ENCI 903 (2022), pp1–2: Sicilian sheepfold/flock guarding, historically wolves and currently foxes and stray dogs; familiar-human docility and attachment, stranger wariness and calmness with entrusted animals. Page 2 also describes nighttime threats toward intruders approaching the sheepfold or property, especially when the dogs are in a group. Goats and a nighttime shelter schedule are not stated. The public copy uses only the supported character and sheepfold/flock role.

VBO:0201459.summary: Lively and steadfast in guarding, the Pastore della Sila is strongly attached to its shepherd. It can be more receptive to unfamiliar people when that trusted person is present. The breed developed in Calabria’s rugged mountains, where protecting livestock, especially goats, from wolves shaped its working life.
VBO:0201459.shortDescription: A devoted Calabrian livestock guardian, shaped by mountain work protecting flocks and goats.

sources.title: Pastore della Sila — ENCI breed standard
sources.evidence: ENCI904pp1–2/8–9: Calabrian mountain livestock/goat protection from wolves; lively tireless firm guarding, devotion to shepherd and stranger sociability in shepherd presence. Local ENCI standard, no FCI-recognition inference.

VBO:0200156.summary: Lively, intelligent and receptive to learning, the Berger de Savoie brings stamina and agility to flock work. It also has a pronounced sense of its own territory, and some dogs can be wary of unfamiliar people. Alpine farms used this versatile helper to move cattle, sheep and goats; architect Marcelle Brüder began selecting the local population during the 1950s.
VBO:0200156.shortDescription: A lively, receptive Alpine herder, agile and enduring at flock work, with a marked sense of its own territory.

sources.title: Société Centrale Canine — Berger des Alpes et de Savoie, national standard537
sources.evidence: Actual complete4pp standard30March2019 personally read: intelligent/lively/receptive/adaptable, territorial and some waryofstrangers; enduring/agile flockwork; Alpinefarmcattle/sheep/goats and MarcelleBrüder selecting1950s. ExplicitFrench national nonFCIstatus. Neolithicskull/ancientlineage or individualfamily/safety promises excluded.

VBO:0200777.summary: Lively and cheerful, the Kokoni combines a loyal companion’s character with an alert side. In Greece it has also been used to sound the alarm and watch small domestic animals. Those modest guarding duties sit alongside companionship in a breed found across the country.
VBO:0200777.shortDescription: A lively, cheerful Greek companion with an alert side, also used to watch small domestic animals.

sources.title: Kennel Club of Greece — Kokoni breed standard
sources.evidence: Actual Greek ΧΡΗΣΙΜΟΤΗΤΑ states companion, alarm dog and guardian of small domestic animals; ΣΥΜΠΕΡΙΦΟΡΑ / ΧΑΡΑΚΤΗΡΑΣ states lively, cheerful, intelligent and loyal; origin states found across Greece. Public prose uses lively/cheerful/loyal, alarm and small-animal work. Ancient continuous ancestry, intelligence ranking, training/child/suitability/health guarantees excluded. National Greek standard; FCI group heading is not international recognition proof.

sources.evidence: Actual 2025 show body has Breed KOKONI and entrant THE KOKONIANS ALIKI. Establishes current maintained identity/registry activity only; not source of temperament, not identity proof for the reference dog.

VBO:0200558.summary: Docile and self-assured, Garafian Shepherds tend to look calm off duty but become very active when herding. Their flock work includes independent decisions as well as following the shepherd’s directions. The breed was preserved in isolated parts of La Palma, especially the pastoral area around Garafía.
VBO:0200558.shortDescription: A self-assured La Palma herder, calm off duty and active in flock work that calls for initiative.

sources.title: Pastor Garafiano — Real Sociedad Canina de España breed standard
sources.evidence: RSCE utilization: independent decisions while guiding flocks beyond the shepherd’s directions. General appearance/character: docile and self-assured, quiet-looking away from work, very active while working. Historical summary: La Palma isolation and pastoral Garafía preserved the breed. No individual suitability guarantee or exaggerated trainability claim. Morphology evidence RSCE sections2–9: small conical head, muzzle/skull4:6, black nose/oblique honey eyes; upright natural ears or forward-folding tips, never foldingfrombase; slightlyraisedcroup≤3cm, abundantfawn/wolfshadedcoat and fullhockreachingbushytail neveroverback. Section7 explicitlyoval compactforefeet and hare-likehindfeet, distinctfront/rearfoottypes.

VBO:0200669.summary: Alert and closely attached to its person, the Hierran Wolfdog can be wary of strangers. Its agility serves a practical job: moving and watching over sheep and goats on El Hierro’s rough ground. Local shepherds have preserved this Canary Islands dog for useful herding work; its deeper ancestry remains uncertain despite its wolf-like outline.
VBO:0200669.shortDescription: An alert El Hierro herding dog, closely bonded to its person and agile on rough ground, with uncertain deeper origins.

sources.title: RSCE — Lobito Herreño standard
sources.evidence: Actual current RSCE history and temperament: largest population in ElHierro with otherCanaryIslands individuals; traditional small-livestock herding, loyal tohandler and waryofstrangers; origins unclear and no pre-conquest descent claim. Conformation: medium lean wolf-like dog, triangular wedgehead, long narrowmuzzle, small triangularprickears, slimmediumbone, straight slightlydescendingtopline, seasonalcoatvariation, common grey with pale mouth/eye surrounds and broad dark-tippedtail. Typicalsize numbers are populationguide, not measured referenceheight. No wolf-hybrid ancestry, individual behavior guarantee or FCIrecognition claim.

No documentaryproof forpre-conquestancestry; author explicitly calls descent claims speculative. Historicalcensus/conservation comments are not2026count, noindividualmeasurements or modernwolf-hybrid claim.

VBO:0200030.summary: Independent and persistent on a scent trail, the American Blue Gascon Hound can be reserved with strangers yet affectionate with familiar people. Raised and hunted in packs on deer and raccoons, it is described as sociable with other dogs. This old-style American hound is valued for a steady tracking pace and a melodious voice.
VBO:0200030.shortDescription: An independent, persistent American scent hound, known for a steady trail pace, a melodious voice and pack hunting.

sources.title: Continental Kennel Club — American Blue Gascon Hound current history and breed standard
sources.evidence: Actual complete CKC history, temperament and conformation body read. Independent/persistent scent-trail behavior, reserved or indifferent with strangers and affectionate/loyal with family, pack raising/hunting and sociability with dogs are current documented tendencies. History documents deer/raccoon packs, steady pace and melodious voice; precise deeper ancestry is explicitly uncertain, and speculative Washington/Acadian descent is not adopted. Standard independently supplies developed moderate sturdy hound proportions, elongated head/full muzzle, long natural drop ears, strong straight back, fore/rear limb geometry, compact arched feet, full tapering natural tail and short blue-roan/ticked coat with possible tan. No individual behavior, safety, health, measured pedigree/age/size or FCI claim.

VBO:0008063.summary: Friendly toward people, Donggyeongi are noted in a Korean agricultural account for their standing jumps. These Gyeongju native dogs have a history documented in old writings and Silla clay figures. Today, conservation programs maintain individual histories and pedigrees to preserve the breed.
VBO:0008063.shortDescription: A people-friendly Gyeongju native dog, noted for standing jumps and preserved through a managed conservation program.

sources.title: Korean native dogs — Rural Development Administration Nongsaro, 2018 transcript
sources.evidence: Actual national agricultural portal2018 transcript, collaborating National Institute of Animal Science, explicitly identifies Donggyeongi as friendly toward people and notes standing vertical jumps. The claim that lack of tail caused hindleg development is omitted, as are individual guarantees and generic Jindo bravery/loyalty traits from the previous separate segment.

sources.evidence: Actual source description HTML referenced by current heritage main page: old Donggyeong japgi/Jeungbo munheon bigo records, Silla clay figures, native Korean breed, usually very short or absent tail, systematic individual-history/breeding/pedigree conservation. No uninterrupted ancient pedigree or present population count claimed.

VBO:0200830.summary: Lively and people-oriented, the Llewellin Setter combines a desire for human attention with strong field instincts. It belongs to the performance strain descended from Purcell Llewellin's nineteenth-century English Setters, selected to locate and point upland birds. In 2021, UKC said it would retain the Field Dog Stud Book’s rules and DNA checks for registration under the Llewellin name.
VBO:0200830.shortDescription: A lively, people-oriented setter from a documented performance strain, selected to locate and point upland birds.

sources.title: Llewellin Setter – Continental Kennel Club Breed Standard
sources.evidence: Named Llewellin own Temperament active/lively/intelligent/people-oriented, attention/affection withstrongfieldinstincts. History directdescendantsPurcellLlewellin mid19thcentury selected performance versusbenchtype; locate/pointuplandgame.

sources.title: UKC / American Field Follow-up Article
sources.evidence: UKC own2021 registry transition statement preserves FDSB Llewellin registration rules and DNAverification; dogsnotverifiedinaccordancewithrulesnotregisteredasLlewellin. This is lineage boundary, not allfieldEnglishSetters.

VBO:0201028.summary: Lively and attached to its handler, the Podenco Valenciano combines some independence with cooperative work alongside other dogs. Its rabbit search alternates air scent with short stretches of ground tracking, restarting a lost trail when needed. A few dry barks alert the hunter to a rabbit hidden close by; the dog gives voice on seeing its quarry.
VBO:0201028.shortDescription: A lively Spanish rabbit hunter, mixing air scent and ground tracking with a distinctive bark to alert its handler.

sources.title: Podenco Valenciano — Royal Canine Society of Spain breed standard
sources.evidence: Actual own RSCE breed standard classifies Group11 national non-FCI. Appearance describes lively/dynamic handler attachment; main role rabbit hunting across Mediterranean, especially eastern Spain/Ebro. Head/ears/body/tail/coat clauses support morphology. Speculative ancient/oldest origin and absolute heat/endurance claims excluded.

sources.title: Working Trial Regulations for Podenco Valenciano — RSCE (approved November 30, 2022)
sources.evidence: Actual working-standard PDFpp14–16: follows track, restarts lost trail, alternates brief ground tracking and air scent; p15 dry bark when hidden quarry is very close and voice only upon seeing it; p16 some independence and cooperation alongside other dogs. Describe working tendencies without individual guarantee.

sources.title: Third Working Cup for Podencos — RSCE results (2025)
sources.evidence: Actual RSCE2025 results name current Podenco Valenciano trial participants, supporting ongoing working continuity only; no population or universal ability claim.

VBO:0201463.summary: Quick in pursuit, the Xigou belongs to China’s local sighthound traditions. In Shaanxi’s Guanzhong region, keepers described seasonal hare coursing around Pucheng and Fuping, crossing open farmland with their dogs. CKU documented living Shaanxi dogs through identification and registration in Xi’an in 2017.
VBO:0201463.shortDescription: A regional Chinese sighthound with a tradition of seasonal hare coursing in Shaanxi’s open farmland.

sources.title: China Daily — Huo Yan, Guanzhong seasonal hare-coursing field report (2018)
sources.evidence: Complete original Chinese field report by named Shaanxi bureau reporter/photographer Huo Yan, March23,2018. Describes agile hunting dogs, local PanZhongxing/Pucheng and native hare-coursing tradition around Pucheng/Fuping; LiuShenglong describes seasonal outings twelfth/first lunar months. Distinguishes native old local dogs from introduced Russian/Australian coursing dogs; never equate every participant/photo with native Xigou or transfer imported-dog speed/endurance. Legends/royalorigin/noharm/intelligence guarantees excluded.

sources.evidence: Actual complete January31,2018 own conservation report: Shaanxi/Xian living dogs at Xi’an April2017 identification/registration, Xianyang September2017 dedicated show. Native local population maintained/documented; not FCIrecognized/2026census or source-dog registration proof.

VBO:0200840.summary: Affectionate and often sensitive, Lurchers tend to enjoy close company, though their energy and confidence vary. Many have a strong instinct to chase and enjoy short bursts of running before relaxing at home. A Lurcher is a sighthound crossed with another dog type, so this name covers many different combinations.
VBO:0200840.shortDescription: A varied sighthound-cross type, often affectionate and sensitive, with a strong chase instinct in many dogs.

VBO:0200745.summary: Watchdog work and finding food along the water shaped the Jonangi’s regional history. Coastal fishermen once kept these dogs in Andhra Pradesh, while accounts from the Godavari basin recall them catching crabs and fish to feed themselves.
VBO:0200745.shortDescription: A coastal Andhra watchdog with Godavari roots and a history of catching crabs and fish for food.

sources.title: Desi mutts — 2009 original report and interview
sources.evidence: Historical coastal watch duties.

The sparse facial skin/coat detail is secondary morphology only; generalized remarks about other Indian breeds are excluded.

VBO:0200356.summary: Affectionate with their people and often vocal, Chiweenies can form close bonds while staying wary of strangers. Their drive for family attention can sit alongside a tenacious streak. This Chihuahua–Dachshund cross can have smooth, long or wiry coats, with substantial individual variation.
VBO:0200356.shortDescription: An affectionate, often vocal Chihuahua–Dachshund cross, with close owner bonds and variable reserve toward strangers.
